chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb and Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah and Dhubyān ibn Ḥakīm, from Mūsā ibn Ukayl al-Numayrī, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayābah, from Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

There is no harm in placing the deceased between your legs and standing over him to wash him. Then when you turn him to the right and to the left, you steady him with your legs so that he does not fall upon his face.

So the import of his statement عليه السلام, 'There is no harm in placing him between your legs,' is to be understood as permissibility and the lifting of prohibition, because the sunnah (prophetic tradition) and what is more virtuous is that one stand at the side of the deceased and not mount over him, as we explained in our major book.

key_terms.الْأَفْضَلَ: that which is more virtuous and preferable
key_terms.الْمَسْنُونَ: that which accords with the sunnah (prophetic tradition)
key_terms.الْمَيِّتَ: the deceased person being prepared and washed
key_terms.تَضْبِطُهُ: to steady and control the body so it does not fall
key_terms.فَتَغْسِلَهُ: to wash him as part of the funeral ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to place the deceased between one's legs while performing ghusl (ritual bath)?
ai.summary: This report addresses the fiqh of washing the deceased, stating that placing the body between one's legs while washing is permissible when needed to keep it from falling. It also clarifies that this wording indicates mere permissibility, while the sunnah (prophetic tradition) and more virtuous practice is to stand at the side of the deceased rather than over him.
